rationale: The Old English verb *a-wegan* (from *wegan*, "to carry, move") is a transitive verb meaning to move or carry something, as evidenced by its attestations in Bosworth-Toller contexts involving physical displacement. Synset move.v.02 ("cause to move or shift into a new position or place") best captures this causative, transitive sense of physical movement, as opposed to intransitive self-motion (travel.v.01) or emotional senses (move.v.11).
